facts.fact: The consolidated National Registration Act (Chapter 01:02, Act 26 of 1986) is an Act of Parliament that commenced on 31 December 1986 and was amended up to Act 11 of 2017 and S.I. 124 of 2017; it provides for the Registrar of National Registration to keep a national register of citizens aged 16 or over and for identity cards to be issued.

facts.fact: The National Registration Act, 1986 (No. 26), an Act of the Parliament of Botswana assented on 24 December 1986, commenced on 31 December 1986 and sets up a national register of citizens and lawfully resident non-citizens aged 16 or over, kept by the Registrar of National Registration, with an identity card issued to each registered person.

The Act requires every applicant to submit to fingerprinting and photographing, requires finger print records to go to the Registrar of National Registration, and gives each registrant a registration number in the national register, so the register it sets up is biometric.

Minister of Labour and Home Affairs Annah Mokgethi presented the National Registration Amendment Bill 2024 to amend the existing National Registration Act, which provides for the Omang identity card.

facts.fact: The National Registration (Amendment) Act 2025 (No. 7), assented 23 March 2025, amends the existing National Registration Act (Cap. 01:02); the amendment starts on a date the Minister sets by Gazette order, not yet stated.
The 2025 amendment, not yet commenced, has the registrar assign a gender-neutral identity number to each person in the Unified Population Register and issue an identity card valid 10 years.
